newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Babcock's Thomassen postpones float again.
newsitem.headline: Babcock's Thomassen postpones float again.

text.p: Dutch gas turbines maker Thomassen International Holding BV said on Friday that it would postpone its planned flotation this autumn because of financial problems at its parent Deutsche Babcock AG.
"It is decided to cancel a bourse introduction for the time being because of restructurings at the shareholder Deutsche Babcock AG," Thomassen said in a statement.
Initially Thomassen planned to float shares in 1995, but later postponed this to June 1996 and then to October 1996.
Deutsche Babcock is currently reforming into a financial holding, aided by a 600 million mark German bank credit line.

"Thomassen, which belongs to (Babcock's) core activities, will be an independent strategic and operational unit. Thomassen will probably be linked directly to the (new Babcock) financial holding," Thomassen said in a statement.
The company also said its managing director Wim Magendans would resign on his own request.
The Dutch company earlier said it had booked a first half net profit of 7.6 million guilders, compared with 4.8 million in the year-ago period.
Turnover was marginally higher at 222.5 million guilders versus 221.6 in the 1995 first half.
But Thomassen's order portfolio had soared to 967 million guilders at the end of June from 796 million a year earlier.
"The order intake over the first six months of 1996 was almost equal to that of the full 1995. Up until now we booked new orders worth of 560 million (this year)," Thomassen said.
